newsitem.title: USA: White House asked if Morris had access to secrets.
newsitem.headline: White House asked if Morris had access to secrets.

text.p: The chairman of the House Intelligence Committee asked on Friday if President Clinton's former political adviser Dick Morris had been given access to classified material at the White House.
In a letter to White House Chief of Staff Leon Panetta, Representative Larry Combest, a Texas Republican, asked if Morris had received security clearance and undergone a background check.
Morris resigned after a supermarket tabloid reported he had had a year-long relationship with a call girl and had allowed her to listen to phone conversations with Clinton.

Combest asked if Morris had taken part in any meetings, briefings or conversations in which classified material had been discussed, if he had had access to classified documents and if he had met on behalf of the United States with foreign nationals.
Combest also asked Panetta if Morris had signed an agreement not to disclose classified information.
